transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... man, my body just feels completely drained. Like, even walking from my car to the clinic just now took everything I have. It's like that at work too, just opening the EHR system takes all my energy. 

We actually just got a new update for the EHR last week. It's supposed to be faster, but they changed all the colors and moved the tabs around, so everyone's just confused. My supervisor, Brenda, was literally screaming at the IT guy on the phone about it yesterday. I felt kind of bad for him, honestly. He's this really quiet guy who always brings donuts on Fridays. The good ones, too, from that bakery next to the gas station. I think they use potato flour or something, makes them super fluffy. 

But yeah... what were we talking about? Oh, right. I'm just so exhausted. It takes everything I have just to do anything right now.
How long have you been feeling this level of exhaustion?

Well, this exhausted part... feeling just totally drained and guilty all the time... it's been going on for about nine months now. It started right after I completely crashed from this period where I had, like, a crazy amount of energy. That was back in the fall, I think? Yeah, because that's exactly when they were repaving the visitor parking lot at the clinic. 

Man, the smell of that hot tar was just everywhere, seeping right into the breakroom windows. My buddy Kyle actually drove his Honda Civic right through the wet asphalt because the construction guys didn't put the orange cones up right. He was so mad. He spent like three hours trying to scrape it off his tires with a plastic butter knife he took from the cafeteria. The cafeteria food is usually pretty terrible anyway, mostly just soggy fries and sad-looking meatloaf, so I don't know why he was even down there. I usually just pack a turkey sandwich, you know? With the spicy mustard. 

But yeah... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. About nine months. Ever since I crashed.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since you started feeling exhausted?

Yeah, sad doesn't even really cover it. After all that energy just... dropped, I started feeling completely empty. Like, just hopeless most days. I keep sitting there thinking I've already completely ruined my future in healthcare before it even really started, you know? Because I just got this clinic job right out of high school. 

My guidance counselor, Mr. Harrison, was actually the one who helped me get the interview. He was this super tall guy who always wore these horrible sweater vests. Like, loud argyle patterns. He actually spilled iced coffee all over a yellow one during my senior exit meeting. It was from that drive-thru place on 4th street that puts way too much ice in the cup. You take like two sips and it's gone. They use those really flimsy paper straws now too, which just melt in your mouth if you don't drink fast enough. I hate that. I mean, I get saving the turtles and everything, but it just tastes like wet cardboard. My sister bought a pack of metal straws, but she lost the little brush to clean them, so now they're just sitting in the kitchen drawer getting gross... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Sorry, my brain is just... yeah. Did you ask if I was sad? Yeah, just really empty.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like before you started feeling exhausted and empty?

No, not really. I used to love playing video games, like, I could spend hours on my PlayStation. But now I just stare at the screen and it feels like too much work to even pick up the controller. I actually bought this new controller a few months ago because my old one got stick drift. It was driving me crazy. You know when your character just starts walking to the left for no reason? 

I tried to take it apart to clean it, watched this whole YouTube tutorial by this guy who had these crazy tattoos all over his hands. Like, really intricate geometric stuff. I always wondered how much something like that costs, or if it hurts more on the knuckles. My cousin got a tattoo on his ribs and said he actually cried. He's a big guy too, plays defensive tackle for his college team. They actually made it to the playoffs last year, but then they lost in the first round because their quarterback threw three interceptions. The weather was terrible though, just pouring rain the whole game. The grass was practically mud... 

Wait, what was the question? Did you ask about my hobbies? Yeah, I just don't really care about anything anymore. It's all just... whatever.
Do you often feel anxious or worried?

Anxious? No, not really. I don't think I even have the energy to be worried about anything right now. 

My mom is the one who worries all the time. She's always pacing around the kitchen, especially when our dog gets out. We have this beagle, Buster, and he always digs under the fence in the backyard. The dirt back there is super loose because of this landscaping project my dad started and never finished. He bought all these heavy retaining wall blocks from Home Depot. Did you know they rent out those flatbed trucks by the hour there? The guy at the rental counter had this glass eye that didn't move when he looked at you. It was kind of distracting, honestly. 

Anyway, my dad got the truck but he completely forgot to buy the actual mortar, so the blocks have just been sitting on wooden pallets in our driveway for like two years now. The HOA keeps sending us these passive-aggressive warning letters on this really thick, cream-colored paper. Who even buys paper like that anymore? It feels like a wedding invitation or something. My cousin just got married and they had this massive chocolate fountain at the reception, but some kid dropped a whole marshmallow in it and it completely jammed the motor. It started making this horrible grinding noise... 

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Did you ask about my family? Oh, right, worried. No, I don't really feel anxious. Just too tired to care, I guess.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

No, there's nothing really. Like I said, even the video games are just... I don't care. I don't look forward to anything. 

My mom tried to get me to go to the movies last week to see that new superhero one. She thought it would cheer me up because I used to collect the comic books when I was younger. I had this whole longbox full of them, mostly the ones with the foil covers from the 90s. My uncle gave them to me when he moved out of his apartment. He lived in this really cramped place above a Chinese restaurant, and the whole hallway always smelled like soy sauce and fried garlic. It was actually really good food, though. They had these little fortune cookies that were individually wrapped in plastic, but the plastic was always really hard to tear open. You know when you try to open something and the plastic just stretches instead of ripping? And then you have to use your teeth, which is probably terrible for your enamel. My dentist told me I need to stop grinding my teeth at night. He gave me this mouthguard, but it tastes like weird rubber and makes me drool on my pillow. I had to buy these special silk pillowcases because I read online that cotton ones cause wrinkles, but they just make your head slide around all night...

Sorry, what did you ask? Did you ask about the movies? Yeah, I didn't go. I just don't have anything I want to do.
Are there any small things that still give you some pleasure, like eating your favorite food or taking a warm shower?

Food? No. Even eating is just... I don't know, it's just chewing and swallowing. I used to really like the breakfast burritos from this little cart near the clinic where I work, but now it's just like cardboard. The guy who runs the cart, Hector, he always wears these really bright neon shirts. Like, construction worker orange. He said he wears them because he almost got hit by a delivery truck once when he was pushing the cart across the intersection. Those delivery trucks are crazy, especially the ones for that big online store. They just park right in the bike lane with their hazard lights blinking like that makes it okay. I saw a guy on an electric scooter slam right into the back of one last month. He wasn't wearing a helmet, just this really thick knit beanie. It was like 80 degrees out, I don't know why he was wearing a beanie. My friend works at a clothing store and she said people buy winter hats in the summer all the time now, it's like a fashion thing. She gets a 30% discount, which is nice, but she spends all her money on shoes anyway. She has this whole wall in her apartment just covered in clear plastic shoeboxes... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Showers? No, I don't really care about that either. It's just... I just don't feel anything good right now.
Do you find that your movements or speech have slowed down since you started feeling exhausted?

Slowed down? Yeah, I guess so. People at work were telling me I looked like I was moving in slow motion. I'm a tech at the clinic, and I could feel it too. Like, even just wrapping up a blood pressure cuff and putting it in the basket was taking me way longer than normal. Or if someone asked me a question, it took me forever to just get the words out. 

We have these new digital blood pressure machines, the ones on the rolling stands with the little basket attached. The wheels on mine always get stuck on the threshold between the hallway and exam room three. Exam room three has this weird poster on the wall about the food pyramid, but it's the old one from the 90s with the bread at the bottom. I don't think anyone even follows that anymore. My sister tried going keto for a while and she was just eating blocks of cheese and bacon every day. She said she felt great but her breath smelled terrible, like nail polish remover. She actually works at a nail salon, the one next to the grocery store with the really good bakery. They make these sourdough loaves that are perfectly crunchy on the outside...

Wait, sorry. What were you asking? Oh, speech and moving slow. Yeah, it just takes me a really long time to do anything or answer anyone.
Are there any activities or things that you used to enjoy, but now you don't find pleasure in them?

Enjoy? No, I don't... I mean, I already said I don't care about video games or the movies or anything anymore. It's all just blank. I used to like playing basketball at the park down the street, but the hoops don't even have nets right now. The city came and took them down last month because some kids were hanging on the rims and bent one of them completely sideways. It's ridiculous, they just left it bent like a weird modern art sculpture. There's this one sculpture downtown near the library that looks like a giant metal crumpled up piece of paper. People are always taking pictures in front of it, especially tourists. I don't get why tourists come here in the summer, it's so humid you step outside and instantly need another shower. My air conditioner at home has been making this awful rattling noise, like there's a pebble stuck in the fan blade. I tried to fix it myself with a butter knife and a screwdriver, but the screws were stripped. You know when the little cross on the screw gets all worn down and smooth? Then you're just spinning the screwdriver for nothing. I need to buy one of those special drill bits to get it out, but the hardware store closes at 6 PM, which is exactly when my shift ends, so I can never make it in time... 

What were we talking about? Oh, things I used to enjoy. Yeah, no, there's nothing. Everything just feels pointless.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

I think... didn't we just talk about this? Like I said, I don't care about basketball or movies or anything. I don't know why you're asking me again. It's like when my manager at the clinic asks me if I restocked the gloves, and I literally just told him five minutes ago that I did. He always forgets because he's constantly drinking those huge energy drinks, the ones in the tall black cans with the green claw marks. He leaves the empty cans all over the breakroom table. One time, someone knocked one over and the sticky residue got all over the bottom of my favorite coffee mug. It's this mug my mom got me when I graduated high school, it has a picture of a dog in a lab coat on it. The dog looks exactly like this golden retriever I saw tied up outside the pharmacy yesterday. It was barking at every single car that drove past, especially the red ones. I don't know if dogs can actually see color or if they just see in black and white, but this dog definitely hated red cars. My cousin has a red car, a really old Honda Civic, and the muffler is so loud it sounds like a lawnmower. He refuses to get it fixed because he says it makes the car sound faster. He's always talking about making things faster, he even bought this special keyboard for his computer so he could type faster for his data entry job...

Wait. What did you ask me? Lost interest? Yeah, I mean, I already told you. I just don't care about anything anymore. It's all blank.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight since you started feeling exhausted and empty?

Weight? Yeah, I guess so. I barely wanted food anyway, so I'd just skip lunch and dinner. I didn't even notice until I realized my scrubs were hanging way looser than normal. I wear the navy blue ones because the clinic requires them, but I hate how the fabric feels after you wash it a few times. It gets all stiff and scratchy, especially around the collar. My mom told me to use this specific fabric softener, the one in the pink bottle with the baby on the front, but I keep forgetting to buy it. The grocery store near me reorganized all their aisles last week and now the laundry stuff is next to the pet food. It makes no sense. Why would you put bleach next to dog kibble? Speaking of dogs, my neighbor's pitbull got loose yesterday and was just running up and down the street with a shoe in its mouth. It wasn't even a chew toy, it was a whole Nike sneaker. Looked like a size 10, maybe 11. I wear a size 11, but I only buy New Balances because they have the best arch support for when I'm on my feet all day at the clinic. The floors there are that hard linoleum tile, the kind that always looks shiny even when it's dirty... 

Wait, sorry. Weight. Yeah, I lost weight. My scrubs are baggy because I was basically just drinking coffee and water for a while. Just didn't want to eat.
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide since you started feeling exhausted and empty?

Death? No, I haven't really thought about killing myself or anything like that. I just feel... empty. Like a battery that won't hold a charge anymore. You know when your phone battery gets really old and it says 100%, but then you make one phone call and it instantly drops to 20%? My phone has been doing that lately. It's so frustrating because I rely on it for my alarm to wake up for work. I use this alarm tone called "Radar" and it's the most obnoxious sound in the world, but it's the only thing that gets me out of bed. My roommate hates it. He works night shifts at the warehouse, so he's usually just falling asleep when my alarm goes off. He told me I need to get a different alarm, maybe one of those ones that slowly lights up the room like a sunrise. I saw one at Target the other day, but it was like eighty dollars. Who pays eighty dollars for an alarm clock? You could buy so many other things with that money. Like groceries, or a new pair of scrubs. The scrubs I have now are so faded, they look more like a dusty gray than navy blue. The washing machines in our apartment building are terrible, they barely agitate the water. And someone always leaves their wet clothes sitting in the dryer for hours. It's so inconsiderate. I usually just end up taking their stuff out and putting it on top of the machine, but then they get mad at me... 

Sorry, what was the question? Oh, suicide. No, I haven't had thoughts like that. Just feeling really drained.
Do you feel like your feelings of emptiness and hopelessness are interfering with your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

Work? Yeah, it definitely messed up work. I got to the point where I couldn't even finish my documentation safely, and I couldn't stay focused on any of the patient-support tasks I'm supposed to do. Employee health actually pulled me off the floor and sent me for an emergency evaluation. They said it was a liability, which is a word my manager uses all the time. He says everything is a liability. Like last month, someone spilled apple juice in hallway B and didn't put a wet floor sign down. He went on a twenty-minute rant about liability and lawsuits. He even printed out this whole packet on slip-and-fall statistics and made everyone read it during the morning huddle. The printer in the breakroom is always running out of toner, though, so half the pages were super faded and you couldn't even read the charts. I tried to change the toner cartridge once, but I ended up getting this black powder all over my hands. It took three days to wash off completely. I had to use this heavy-duty pumice soap that my dad uses when he works on his truck. His truck is this massive Ford F-150, it's lifted and has these huge off-road tires even though he literally only drives it to the grocery store and back. He says he likes sitting up high so he can see over traffic, but I think he just likes how loud the engine is. It rumbles so much that when he idles in the driveway, the windows in our living room rattle...

Wait, sorry. Functioning. Yeah, I had to stop working. And I also had to stop preparing for my CNA certification. I was studying for it, but I just couldn't keep up with anything anymore. It's all too much.
Do you feel like your feelings of emptiness and hopelessness are getting worse over time?

Getting worse? I don't know about worse, it's just... it's been going on for a really long time. The depressed, guilty, exhausted part has lasted about nine months now. It started right after I crashed from that really high-energy period I had. That crash was brutal. It felt like hitting a brick wall at sixty miles an hour. Speaking of driving, my car's check engine light came on yesterday and I'm terrified to take it to the mechanic. The last time I went, they tried to tell me I needed a whole new transmission when all I needed was a spark plug. Mechanics always try to upcharge you, especially if you look young or like you don't know anything about cars. My uncle is a mechanic, but he lives all the way out in Oregon, so it's not like I can just drive over to his shop. He owns this huge garage that specializes in vintage European cars. He sent me a picture of this 1960s Porsche he was restoring, and the paint color was this incredible deep emerald green. I tried to find a shirt in that exact color once, but everything I found was either too bright or too dark. It's really hard to find good green clothes that don't make you look like a leprechaun or a park ranger. I ended up just buying a black hoodie instead, because black goes with everything. Plus, you can't see coffee stains on black, and I spill coffee on myself at least twice a week at the clinic...

Oh, wait. You asked about the emptiness getting worse. Yeah, it's just been a steady nine months of feeling exhausted and guilty since that high-energy phase ended. It hasn't really changed, just dragged on forever.
Have you experienced any strange thoughts, heard voices, or seen things that others cannot see since you started feeling exhausted and empty?

Strange thoughts or hearing things? No, not since I've been feeling this exhausted. I mean, all that stuff... the ideas about having some special medical mission, and hearing my name being called, or the heart monitors beeping and calling out to me... that only happened when I was super wired. You know, when I was barely sleeping and trying to completely overhaul the whole clinic system. I was so convinced I had to fix everything. The filing system at the clinic is a disaster, by the way. They still use these manila folders with the color-coded stickers on the edges, but half the stickers fall off because the glue gets old. I tried to reorganize them all alphabetically and by birth year, but then the front desk receptionist got really mad at me. Her name is Brenda, and she's been working there for like thirty years. She has this giant collection of ceramic frogs on her desk. Every time you try to hand her a chart, you have to navigate around these tiny, staring frogs. One of them is wearing a little sombrero. I don't even know where you buy a ceramic frog wearing a sombrero. Maybe at one of those weird roadside tourist traps? My dad took us to one in Florida once when I was a kid. It was supposed to be a gator farm, but it was just a bunch of sad-looking alligators sitting in muddy water. They had a gift shop that smelled like cheap vanilla candles and dust. I bought a mood ring there, but it always stayed black, which meant I was supposedly stressed all the time. I guess the ring was right, considering how things turned out... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the voices and the special mission stuff. Yeah, once that huge high-energy period ended and I crashed, all of that stopped. I haven't been hearing those things or feeling like I was chosen for anything since I've been feeling empty. Just the exhaustion now.
Do you feel like your feelings of emptiness and hopelessness are severe enough to interfere with your daily life almost completely?

Yeah, it really does interfere with everything. Like I was saying, after all that energy dropped, I just started feeling empty and hopeless most days. It honestly feels like I've already ruined my future in healthcare before it even really started. Which is really upsetting because I just spent so much money on these new scrubs. They were the expensive kind, the ones with the extra cargo pockets on the leg. You really need those pockets for all the alcohol swabs and pens. I got them in navy blue because that's the mandatory color for support staff at our clinic. Navy blue is such a boring color, honestly. My mom tried to wash them for me before I wore them, but she accidentally left a tissue or a receipt or something in her own pants pocket in the same load, so my brand new dark scrubs came out completely covered in this white fuzz. We had to use a lint roller on them for like forty-five minutes. Peeling the sticky layers off the lint roller is kind of satisfying, though. My cat hates the lint roller, by the way. His name is Cheddar, he's this fat orange tabby, and the second he sees the roller he bolts right under the sofa. He thinks it's the vacuum cleaner. Our vacuum makes this horrible high-pitched squealing noise because the belt is loose, and my dad refuses to replace it. He says he can just fix it with duct tape, but duct tape doesn't fix a rubber belt...

Wait, sorry. I lost track again. You were asking if the emptiness stops me from functioning. But yeah, that feeling of just being totally hopeless and having ruined my chances at a career... it's severe enough that I can't really do much of anything right now.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or having trouble sitting still, or do you feel like you're moving in slow motion most of the time?

Moving in slow motion? Yeah, definitely slow motion. It's like I'm wading through molasses or something. People at work were actually pointing it out to me. They said I looked really slowed down, and I could totally feel it, too. Like, even just putting a blood pressure cuff away or answering a simple question took me way, way longer than normal. Which is really bad in a clinic, because everything is always go, go, go. You have to turn over those exam rooms so fast. And they use these specific blood pressure cuffs where the Velcro gets all frayed after a few months, and then it doesn't stick right, so you're standing there trying to get a reading while the cuff keeps popping open. It's so embarrassing when the patient is just staring at you. I tried to order new cuffs once, but the medical supply catalog is like a thousand pages long. It's ridiculous. It's thicker than a phone book. Do people even use phone books anymore? I remember my grandma used to use them as booster seats for us at the kitchen table when we were little. Her kitchen always smelled like Pine-Sol and overcooked cabbage. She loved making this weird cabbage soup that had hot dogs cut up in it. I hated it, but she'd make me eat a whole bowl before I could go outside and play. We used to catch lightning bugs in her backyard in these old mayonnaise jars with holes poked in the lid... 

But yeah, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, the slow motion thing. Yeah, I just couldn't move at my normal speed, and everything, even just answering people, took forever.
Do you feel like your feelings of emptiness and hopelessness are getting worse over time or have they stayed about the same?

They've stayed about the same, honestly. It's just been this constant, heavy feeling. The depressed, guilty, exhausted part has lasted for about nine months now, ever since I crashed after that huge high-energy period. Nine whole months. It feels like an eternity when you're just dragging yourself around. I actually marked it on my calendar when I started feeling really bad. It's one of those big desk calendars with the tear-off pages. I got it at an office supply store because they were having a clearance sale. I love office supply stores. All the different colored pens and the sticky notes... I have a serious weakness for sticky notes. I buy them in every shape. I even have some shaped like little apples. I used to stick them all over my locker in high school to remind myself to do my homework, but the adhesive on the apple ones wasn't very strong, so they'd always curl up and fall off into the bottom of my locker. My locker was a total mess anyway. I shared it with this guy named Kevin who played lacrosse, and his gear always smelled like wet dog and old cheese. I don't know how he stood it. He used to leave his cleats right on top of my textbooks...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? But yeah, to answer your question, the emptiness hasn't really gotten worse or better. It's just been a steady nine months of feeling completely drained and guilty since I crashed.
Would you describe your current feelings of emptiness and hopelessness as mildly bothersome, moderately debilitating, or severely incapacitating?

Severely incapacitating, definitely. I mean, it got so bad that I couldn't even finish my documentation safely or stay focused on basic patient-support tasks at the clinic. It was a huge mess. Eventually, employee health just pulled me from work completely and sent me for an emergency evaluation. They were actually really nice about it, the nurse in employee health. Her name was Brenda, I think. She had this huge collection of enamel pins on her lanyard. One of them was a little cartoon brain holding a cup of coffee, which I thought was pretty funny. I used to collect pins when I was younger, mostly ones from different national parks my family visited. We went to Yellowstone once and it smelled so strongly of sulfur, like rotten eggs, everywhere you went near the geysers. My sister complained about it the entire trip. She was going through this phase where she only wore black and listened to these really obscure emo bands. She even painted her nails black, but she'd pick at the polish so it always looked chipped and terrible. She used to blast that music from her bedroom, and the bass would rattle the pictures on the hallway wall. One time, a framed photo of my grandparents actually fell off the wall and the glass shattered everywhere. My dad was so mad, he grounded her for two weeks...

Oh, wait. Right, the emptiness. But yeah, it's severely incapacitating. I also had to completely stop preparing for my CNA certification because I just couldn't keep up with the studying or anything anymore. So yeah, I can't really function at all.

doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

target_item.name: Fatigue
target_item.manifestation: I'm here because my body feels completely drained, like even walking from my car to the clinic or opening the EHR takes everything I have.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code (S029).

patient.answer:
I'm here because... man, my body just feels completely drained. Like, even walking from my car to the clinic just now took everything I have. It's like that at work too, just opening the EHR system takes all my energy. 

We actually just got a new update for the EHR last week. It's supposed to be faster, but they changed all the colors and moved the tabs around, so everyone's just confused. My supervisor, Brenda, was literally screaming at the IT guy on the phone about it yesterday. I felt kind of bad for him, honestly. He's this really quiet guy who always brings donuts on Fridays. The good ones, too, from that bakery next to the gas station. I think they use potato flour or something, makes them super fluffy. 

But yeah... what were we talking about? Oh, right. I'm just so exhausted. It takes everything I have just to do anything right now.

patient.answer:

It started right after I completely crashed from this period where I had, like, a crazy amount of energy. That was back in the fall, I think?
